role.description: Disambiguates multiple payloads of the same type+version that target different MCUs within one multi-MCU device (e.g. KBP4's Central vs Peripheral firmware). Absent/empty means the payload is the family's single primary target for that type - getPayloadPath() only matches role-less payloads unless a specific role is requested, so existing single-MCU families are unaffected. Added 2026-08-15 for KBP4.

versionEncoding.description: How to decode the bootloader/application version bytes in this family's identity reply. 'standard' (default when absent): each version is 3 bytes read straight as major/minor/patch. 'bcd16': legacy QuNeo-era layout - each version is only 2 bytes in the reply, [patch (LSB), (major<<4)|minor as BCD nibbles (MSB)], sent LSB-first, so the bootloader and app versions pack into 4 contiguous bytes instead of 6. A standard parse of that misaligns (the app's patch lands in bl_ver[2]) and BCD-misreads the MSB (e.g. QuNeo 1.2.31 -> '18.0.0'); see kmiDevice::midiCppIDReplyCallback.

requiresFlushAfterPreamble.description: Set true when this family's SysEx preamble parser stops reading at a fixed byte count without regard for the 7-bit/8-bit decode's group boundaries (SX_ENCODE_LEN), so the first payload byte of a sendSyxFormattedMessage()-based command can land in the same decode group as the tail of the preamble and be silently dropped unless the sender flushes after the preamble (SysExMessageTX::setFlush(SYX_FLUSH_YES), or firmware_tester's --flush-after-preamble). Discovered on K-Board; also documented for EM Pro Riser in mk_firmware_tester/lib/midi_cpp's own source comments.

firmwareUpdateDefaults.description: Per-family default chunking/delay profile applied automatically by sendsysex's --fw-update for this family, letting a small fast first window clear the host before a receiver that starts a blocking operation (e.g. a flash erase) as soon as it sees the message header, then settle with a longer gap before the rest of the transfer proceeds at its own steady-state size/delay. Absent means --fw-update uses the tool's ordinary CLI defaults (-cs 512 -cd 100 -pd 500, -fcs/-fgd disabled) for this family, same as before this field existed. Any of these values still lose to an explicit CLI flag (-fcs/-fgd/-cd/-pd) if the user passes one. Added 2026-08-18, generalized from a KBP4-only hardcode - see kbp4.json for the field-by-field rationale.

firstChunkSize.description: Bytes. Overrides -cs for the very first sub-split window of the first chunk only. 0/absent disables the override.

firstGapDelayMs.description: Milliseconds. Overrides -cd for the single gap following that first window only. 0/absent disables the override.

chunkDelayMs.description: Milliseconds. Default -cd, the minimum wait after sending a chunk before demanding its identity reply (pure pacing - does not affect how long a reply is waited for). Absent leaves the tool's normal -cd default (100). Split 2026-08-25 from also doubling as the reply-wait budget; see idReplyTimeoutMs.

postDelayMs.description: Milliseconds. Default -pd, the wait after the last chunk before closing the port. Absent leaves the tool's normal -pd default (500).

idReplyTimeoutMs.description: Milliseconds. Default --id-reply-timeout: how long one identity-request attempt waits for a reply before it's considered silent. Absent/0 leaves the tool's normal default (300). Added 2026-08-25.

idReplyResendAttempts.description: Default --id-reply-resend-attempts: how many additional times to resend the identity request and wait idReplyTimeoutMs again after a silent chunk, before the chunk (and then the whole transfer) is considered failed. Absent/0 leaves the tool's normal default (2). Added 2026-08-25.

appRebootMaxAttempts.description: Maximum number of 1-second poll iterations to wait for the device to return to application mode after a firmware transfer. Absent/0 leaves the hardcoded fallback (60). Added 2026-08-27.

rebootsToAppOnFinalChunk.description: When true, the device reboots straight into application mode as it commits the final firmware chunk and never answers an identity request on the bootloader port afterwards. --fw-update skips the doomed final-chunk bootloader handshake and relies on its application-port reconnect + version check as the success test, avoiding ~9s of waiting for a reply that structurally cannot come. Absent/false keeps the historical behavior (wait postDelayMs for a final bootloader reply). Added 2026-08-26.

confirmByAppReconnectOnly.description: When true, --fw-update confirms success by application-mode reconnect alone and skips the post-update version match. For families whose application firmware does not answer the standard Universal Device Inquiry (e.g. MalletStation / EM Pro Riser, which report version only via a proprietary OSC-over-SysEx message), an identity request in application mode never replies so a version match is impossible; reconnecting on the application port (detected by port name) is the success signal - a device still stuck in the bootloader shows its bootloader port instead. Absent/false keeps the strict version-match confirmation. Added 2026-08-26.
